PullRequest.Title: Folder Location and chat area: provider rows keep their identity, Close All keeps the last-used draft first across groups
PullRequest.Body:

## What

Follow-up to #348882, fixing two review findings that landed after it merged.

## Changes

- **Folder Location picker** (`folderLocationStatusBar.ts`): a group row's id is its provider's id, not its label. Two providers can share a label such as "Worktrees", and the action widget keeps an open submenu on the first row with the same id. Before this, refreshing the locations could move an open submenu to another provider's locations. `IFolderLocationGroup` now carries `providerId`, which `getLocationGroups` fills in; the row shown before the lookup finishes uses the current location's `providerId`.
- **Close All** (`agentsChatPart.ts`): the chat part remembers which of its tabs were active last, across its groups. Close All collects the drafts that composers keep as they close (only on a successful close) and keeps them least recently used first. In Single, New Chat then brings back the draft of the composer used last, also when it is in a group used less recently or sits behind another chat. Before this, drafts were kept in the order the groups closed, which was creation order. A tab moving between the part's groups (a close with `EditorCloseContext.MOVE`) is still open: it no longer keeps its draft, which came back twice, nor loses when it was active.

## Notes for reviewers

- The label stays presentation only. In Multiple, Close All still keeps no drafts.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` agentsChatPart (54), folderLocationStatusBar and workspaceFolderLocationService (33): all passing, 0 failing. Without the fixes, the new tests fail: same-label providers; Close All with the composer used last in another group, behind a chat in a group used more recently, or moved to another group. Two tests now expect the provider id.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 2022 passing, 0 failing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/workbench/{contrib/workspaces,services/workspaces}/test/**/*.test.js"`: 185 passing, 0 failing

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: In Single mode, moving a nonempty unsent composer between chat-part groups fired the ordinary close handlers, which captured its draft and appended it to _kept although the same composer stayed open in the target. Repeated moves accumulated duplicate entries without consuming them. _save/_writeStored exported attachments and serialized every entry, so m moves of a draft of serialized size d added O(m*d) serialization and stored bytes; editing between moves could also retain distinct historical snapshots.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Statically established accumulation of duplicate kept drafts across moves, with increasing save-time allocation/serialization and persisted state; reloading also materializes the duplicate drafts. No measured timings are claimed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added MOVE guards skip both draft capture and the kept-draft append for a transfer, preserving the live composer and retaining its draft only when it actually closes.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: EditorGroupView.doMoveOrCopyEditorAcrossGroups opens the same input in the target before closing it in the source with EditorCloseContext.MOVE (editorGroupView.ts:1603-1607); handleOnDidCloseEditor still fires close events but does not dispose an input open elsewhere (lines 719-746). The deleted base line 856 appended the captured draft unconditionally, and no move path pops _kept. The new guards at agentsChatPart.ts:862 and :875 bypass this. _captureClosingComposerInput/_sendableComposerInput (909-931) show that nonempty unsent drafts qualify; _writeStored (986-994) maps every kept entry through toStoredChatDraft and stringify, and newChatDraftState.ts:39-44 exports all attachments. The added movedD case at agentsChatPart.test.ts:1302-1311 corroborates retaining the moved draft only once. Blame identifies the introducing commit for the old append.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Folder Location picker from the status bar or command, including an alternate current location and providers sharing a label.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The seeded picker renders immediately; getLocationGroups resolves later and updates its rows once. The built-in worktree provider returns currently known locations without awaiting host listing or realpath.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the primary workspace folder's real path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one outstanding lookup per normalized workspace-folder key; a successful result is reused. A rejected lookup is evicted and can retry on a subsequent request. No lookup per displayed worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical lookup, key, caching, and scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started in the background by provideLocations/getFolderForms; not awaited before displaying the picker or known locations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List the enabled local agent host's sessions through one root listSessions request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced request per invalid host-list cache, not per session, agent, or picker row; none for a valid warm cache or unavailable/disabled host. Failed listings remain retryable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider enumeration already started the same background host listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background during picker enumeration; later provider notifications expose newly known worktrees.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P registered providers, S cached host sessions, and L distinct offered locations after URI deduplication. The current built-in implementation is one worktree provider; extensible grouping remains one provideLocations call per registered provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing Promise.all across P providers; the built-in provider coalesces its host listing and folder lookup independently. One asynchronous picker refresh per command invocation, with cancellation on dismissal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The location service itself does not cache getLocationGroups. Its provider retains normalized folder forms and a notification-maintained, in-flight-coalesced session list. Adding providerId neither changes cache keys nor invalidation or negative-result behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both modified mapping sites only carry provider.id into existing objects, and the changed row id is consumed by existing widget refresh logic. Boundary counts and scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider counts and history sizes vary; no runtime measurements were available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression: provider identity changes row matching, not enumeration, allocation cardinality, or I/O frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a resolved alternate folder location or return to the primary folder.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command awaits setFolderLocation. Alternate selection resolves its provider, settles trust, and queues configuration initialization before the switch completes; returning to primary skips alternate resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await the primary folder's realpath forms when validating an alternate location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero additional reads on a warm folder key, otherwise one shared lookup for that primary folder, not per offered location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same resolution path and folder cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the host's session list if the requested location is not yet known.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced cold listing at a time; refresh is a no-op with a valid list cache. Providers are checked sequentially until resolution succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The selected URI was already passed into this same resolver. providerId on picker rows does not add a resolver or bypass grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold missing-location resolution awaits the shared listing; warm known locations return without it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and store trust state if the selected destination receives a new trust grant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Conditional on a trust change for the single chosen destination; not repeated for all picker entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical trust lookup and grant behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Trust grant completes before applying that destination.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize configuration for the single selected workspace folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration-initialization operation per applied, changed destination, reusing existing configuration caches; no initialization for each offered location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical configuration work and queue placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited inside the workspace-editing queue before the switch completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-selected destination, up to P sequential provider resolutions, and the host's S cached sessions; not L switches for L offered locations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider resolution is sequential. Concurrent requests use existing freshness checks; application of workspace edits is serialized by workspaceEditingQueue. Host listings coalesce globally within the provider's list store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing folder-form and host-list caches remain effective. Trust/configuration state is managed by unchanged authoritative services. Selecting the current folder still uses the existing no-change configuration shortcut.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the unchanged selected-URI command path through workspace editing, provider resolution, trust persistence, and queued configuration initialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold filesystem/configuration latency and session-list size are deployment-dependent, but none of these boundary mechanisms is changed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the diff changes provider-row identity without adding or moving any selection-time boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate, individually close, or move chat/composer tabs between chat-part groups.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation updates existing observables and then the new recency array synchronously. A normal successful close removes the input from recency. A move opens the same input in its target group before emitting source close events.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N currently open chat-part inputs. Recency updates/filtering cost O(N) references per actual active-input transition or successful close, not per keystroke or render frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event callbacks; redundant updateActive calls return before allocating when the active input is unchanged. Moves are handled as target-open then source-close, rather than as independent draft closures.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _recentInputs deduplicates inputs on activation, removes them on actual close, and clears on part shutdown. MOVE preserves the entry because the input stays open; input move restrictions prevent escape to an untracked part. Draft capture uses the existing in-memory composer snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lifecycle cleanup, move restrictions, and event ordering were inspected. No subprocess, network, filesystem, or database operation is added to the changed callbacks; persistence occurs on the separate save path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or large-tab-count profiles were available. The added linear array bookkeeping is evident but does not establish a meaningful regression for realistic interactive tab counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No qualifying introduced regression. The MOVE guards also fix duplicate draft retention, recorded separately through report_regression_fix with blame provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Close All in Single or Multiple chat-tabs mode across one or several groups.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Snapshot group/tab recency, close groups, then append successfully captured drafts in sorted order before the command resolves. Both the old closeEditors path and new closeAllEditors path close inactive editors before the active editor, avoiding intermediate activation/rendering of every hidden chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily read and parse the stored chat-part state if kept drafts have not been initialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one parse per lazy initialization, served from the storage service's cached value; warm calls do not parse again. Multiple mode initializes _kept to an empty array in the constructor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Close All with captured drafts already initialized the same kept state; a no-capture close did not force that initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new finally block initializes kept state even when this invocation captured no drafts. Previously initialization happened here only through a captured composer; saving/opening a composer also already initialized it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: G groups and N open inputs; recency contains at most roughly 2N references. Only K successfully closed, nonempty, unsent Single-mode composers are sorted. Multiple mode captures none. Typical Single use has few unsent composers, although restored drafts can increase K.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all across G group closures existed before and remains. Confirmation handling is sequential within each group and coalesces pending confirmations. Actual editor disposal is synchronous within each resolved group closure. Sorting is synchronous after closures, using linear rank lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing kept drafts remain lazily initialized once. The new recency snapshot and capture array live only for this Close All invocation; _closingAllKept is cleared in finally. No new persistent cache or per-editor boundary call is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High on exact scheduling, cardinality, temporary ownership, and before/after behavior; insufficient evidence of meaningful degradation from the bounded interactive bookkeeping to justify a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sorting is O(N*K*log K) and per-close recency filtering adds array work; no realistic large-K trigger or measured user-visible cost was established. The extra cold parse is a one-time initialization of existing state, without demonstrated material cost in the reviewed workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance regression. Existing bulk-close batching is preserved, and draft ordering only processes successful captures.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist and restore drafts after moving a nonempty unsent composer between chat-part groups.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Moves update in-memory state. onWillSaveState later synchronously exports drafts and serializes chat-part state; storage backend flushing is deferred. Subsequent restoration parses the saved drafts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Export attachment payloads and serialize/parse all retained drafts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One chat-part serialization per save, proportional to total retained draft bytes. Before the fix, M moves could add M duplicate draft entries, adding O(M*D) serialized bytes for draft size D. The MOVE guards now add zero kept entries for transfers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serialization boundary existed, but its payload grew with duplicate drafts accidentally appended on every move.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization runs synchronously on the save callback and parsing during restoration; not directly during the move.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist pending storage updates through database.updateItems.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Storage updates are cached and coalesced by key in pendingInserts, then flushed in a throttled batch. Not one database write per tab move. Avoiding duplicate drafts reduces the stored value's size rather than changing batching cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deferred flush behavior, carrying the unnecessarily enlarged draft value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Backend flush is deferred from the synchronous chat-part serialization callback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M moves of an unsent composer, serialized draft size D including exported attachments, and the number of genuinely parked or closed drafts. Editing between moves could previously retain distinct historical snapshots as well.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Moves and draft appends are synchronous event work; serialization occurs once per save event. Database flushing uses the existing throttled/coalesced storage mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the fix, _kept retained each duplicate until consumed or cleared, and persistence recreated duplicates after reload. The fix skips capture/append for MOVE without changing normal closed-draft retention, lazy loading, or storage batching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced target-open/source-MOVE-close ordering, the deleted unconditional kept-draft append, export/stringify and restore paths, and storage coalescing. blame_base_line resolved the old append to commit 3b381b139291d9bbdd5a5a1ae60d41dad26d137d.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The accumulation and serialization scaling are statically established; the frequency of repeated moves and actual attachment sizes were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: This is a fixed pre-existing performance mechanism, not a new finding. Submitted one internal regression-fix record for unbounded duplicate-draft retention and its save/restore cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. Traced folder-picker enumeration/selection, chat activation/moves/cleanup, bulk closure, and draft persistence with effective caches and concurrency. No high-confidence introduced performance findings qualified. Recorded one concrete duplicate-draft retention fix with base-line blame provenance. Static read-only review; no runtime profiling.
